intervals.label: operation
intervals.note: End date from the Belle collaboration's legacy page: 'KEKB/Belle operation successfully ended on 30-June-2010.' The KEK accelerator page says 'KEKB concluded its operation in June 2010'. Construction and design intervals are not recorded: no source fetched in this session gives them.

intervals.label: shut down for the SuperKEKB upgrade
intervals.note: Terminal event. KEKB was not dismantled but rebuilt in place as SuperKEKB.

name: KEKB
notes: Construction and commissioning intervals are missing: no fetched source gives KEKB construction start or first-beam dates.
The KEKB linac injector is not modelled here; it belongs to facility:kek.

beam_energy.note: Asymmetric energies: 8 GeV in the high-energy (electron) ring, 3.5 GeV in the low-energy (positron) ring.
beam_energy.quote: It collides 3.5 GeV positrons and 8 GeV electrons at the interaction point

circumference.note: The quoted figure is the Belle II collaboration's description of SuperKEKB, which was built in the KEKB tunnel and reuses the same ring; no source fetched in this session states the KEKB circumference directly.

integrated_luminosity.note: Lower bound delivered/recorded over the whole KEKB programme; the legacy Belle page states 'greater than 1000 fb^-1', i.e. about 1 ab⁻¹.

peak_luminosity.note: World record for a colliding-beam accelerator until the LHC passed it in 2018; KEK's 2020 press release quotes the same KEKB value, 2.11×10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹. The KEKB ring page rounds it to 2.1×10³⁴.
peak_luminosity.quote: World Record Luminosity of 2.11 x 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ achieved in June 2009 with crab cavities at KEKB

summary.plain: A three-kilometre-long machine at the KEK laboratory in Japan that smashed electrons into positrons at different energies from 1998 to 2010. It made huge numbers of B mesons for the Belle experiment and set a world record for collision rate.
summary.technical: Asymmetric-energy e⁺e⁻ double-ring collider (8 GeV HER × 3.5 GeV LER) operating on the Υ(4S) resonance, 3 km circumference; peak luminosity 2.11×10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ with crab cavities, more than 1 ab⁻¹ integrated.
